content: Even a creature an inch long possesses half an inch of soul.
author: Japanese Proverbs
sourceWork: Issun no mushi ni mo gobu no tamashii (一寸の虫にも五分の魂)
explanation: No being, regardless of how small or seemingly insignificant, is devoid of life's sacred impulse. Rooted in Buddhist and Shinto reverence for all forms of consciousness, this proverb warns against arrogance toward the small, the vulnerable, and the overlooked.
practicalInsight: Treat the lowliest service worker, the quietest child, or a passing insect with the same dignity you would offer an emperor.
reflectionPrompt: How does your demeanor shift when interacting with people who can offer you nothing in return?
